evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Ensure data quality, reliability, and freshness through testing, monitoring, and validation
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by quality, testing, monitoring, and reliability language with no velocity/speed phrases present, so rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: You will enable teams through reliable data models, standardized metrics, and strong data quality, working on large-scale datasets for a global product used by billions of users worldwide.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect internal business decisions and product analytics at scale but there is no explicit financial reporting, regulatory, or compliance language, so moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: BI platform team; BI data science unit
evidence.data_team_maturity: Join our BI team and help us shape the business decisions and processes of TeamViewer... You will work with our BI platform team with the BI data science unit.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Multiple named, specialised data sub-teams (BI platform team, BI data science unit) already exist within a company of 1,900+ employees, indicating a mature, established data function.
evidence.jd_authorship: Optimize data warehouse pipelines and processes to efficiently handle large-scale datasets for a product used by 2+ billion users worldwide
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities cite a precise scale figure (2+ billion users) and specific technical activities (on-call rotations, post-mortems, data warehouse pipelines), giving a concrete picture of the day-to-day work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Act as a key interface between platform analytics and data consumers, understanding their needs and translating them into reusable data assets
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role is framed around serving internal data consumers and platform analytics with reusable data assets and standardized metrics, making internal_data the dominant orientation.
evidence.autonomy_level: Maintain and improve data applications that optimize various business processes; Act as a key interface between platform analytics and data consumers, understanding their needs and translating them into reusable data assets
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Responsibilities are framed as maintaining, improving, and translating others' needs into deliverables rather than setting direction, which is execution-oriented.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI is mentioned only in the company description ("harness the power of AI and shape the future of digitalization") and not as a skill or tool expected of the candidate.
evidence.testing_framing: Ensure data quality, reliability, and freshness through testing, monitoring, and validation
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and data quality are framed as a responsibility the candidate owns and executes, not merely a tool in a requirements list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Diagnose and resolve data issues and outages, participate in on-call rotations, contribute to post-mortems, and proactively suggest improvements to engineering excellence
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Moderate: the fear framing centers on operational reliability (outages, on-call, post-mortems) rather than compliance or regulatory risk, which is secondary to delivery.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Maintain and improve data applications that optimize various business processes; Optimize data warehouse pipelines and processes to efficiently handle large-scale datasets
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by maintain/improve/optimize verbs applied to existing data applications and pipelines rather than building new ones from scratch.
evidence.language_gate: Fluency in English with strong communication skills
evidence.work_arrangement: Hybrid and Flexible work time with up to 50% home office
evidence.loss_aversion: Diagnose and resolve data issues and outages, participate in on-call rotations, contribute to post-mortems, and proactively suggest improvements to engineering excellence — reflects a fear of operational/pipeline reliability failures rather than compliance risk.
